content.title: Rory McIlroy has won his second Masters – but not another Green Jacket
content.text: Rory McIlroy has achieved a rare Masters double – but one Augusta tradition often gets misunderstood.The Northern Irishman successfully defended his title at The Masters to join one of the most exclusive clubs in the game.Only Jack Nicklaus, Nick Faldo and Tiger Woods had successfully gone back-to-back at Augusta National Golf Club. Only Faldo has successfully defended his maiden title. McIlroy also becomes just the 19th man to win the Masters more than once.But in seeing out victory on Sunday, does he actually get another Green Jacket?It’s one of the most common Masters misconceptions.Do Masters winners get a new Green Jacket every time?No – not in the way most people think.The Green Jacket isn’t a trophy that stacks up with each victory. Instead, each champion effectively has one jacket associated with them.When a player wins the Masters for the first time, they are fitted for their own Green Jacket (38 regular, “European” fit – slightly more tailored, tapered, and pinched in – in McIlroy’s case). That jacket is theirs to take home for a year and wear as they wish. Hands up if you’d be wearing it on the school run! Then it must be returned to Augusta National, where it stays. From that point on, it lives at the club – ready to be put into the champion’s locker whenever they return to the sacred ground.Like this article? Click here to add Today’s Golfer as a preferred source on Google.What happens if they win the Masters again? McIlroy’s win in 2026 doesn’t suddenly double his wardrobe.At the Butler Cabin ceremony, chairman Fred Ridley placed the Green Jacket on his shoulders – and crucially, it was his jacket, not a different one.“It still fits,” McIlroy quipped at the ceremony. Augusta National maintain and adjust jackets over time, and if a player’s size drastically changes, a new one may be made, but that’s about fit, not building a collection.Jack Nicklaus and Tiger Woods don’t have a rail of Green Jackets waiting for them. They have one that has evolved with them.Where did the Green Jacket come from?The Green Jacket wasn’t always part of the Masters story.The idea came from Bobby Jones, who was struck by the red jackets worn by officials at Royal Liverpool Golf Club in 1927. He liked the authority it gave – something he felt American golf lacked.When Augusta National Golf Club opened in 1933, Jones and Clifford Roberts explored the idea, eventually settling on green – inspired by the azalea-lined grounds.Members first wore the jackets during the Masters in 1937 so patrons could easily identify them. A lighter version followed a year later, and the tradition stuck.The color is officially Masters Green (Pantone 342).How do they get the right size on Sunday?There’s a simple solution behind the Butler Cabin moment.With players ranging from Gary Player to George Archer in size, Augusta National identify members of a similar build to the leaders early on Sunday. Their jackets are used for the presentation.Once the winner is confirmed, the closest match is selected for the ceremony, photos and interviews – which is why the fit isn’t always perfect.The champion is then measured and fitted for their own jacket in the weeks that follow.Why all of this mattersThey’re small details, but say everything about Augusta.The Green Jacket isn’t about accumulation or display – it’s about perfection and belonging. Once you’ve won, you’re part of the club, you’ll get the perfect fit, and your jacket stays there with you.Which means if McIlroy does make history again this week, he won’t walk away with a second jacket.He’ll simply reinforce ownership of the one that already defines his place at Augusta.
